recommendations.text: Measure cardiac troponins with high-sensitivity assays immediately after presentation and obtain results within 60 minutes of blood sampling.
Use an ESC algorithmic approach with serial hs-cTn measurements (0 h/1 h or 0 h/2 h) to rule in and rule out NSTEMI.
Additional testing after 3 h is recommended if the first two hs-cTn measurements of the 0 h/1 h algorithm are inconclusive and no alternative diagnoses explaining the condition have been made.
Consider use of established risk scores (e.g., GRACE risk score) for prognosis estimation.

Triage for emergency reperfusion strateg.recommendation: Patients with suspected STEMI should be immediately triaged for an emergency reperfusion strategy.

3.3.1 High-sensitivity cardiac troponins.recommendation: Measurement of a biomarker of cardiomyocyte injury, preferably high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn), is recommended in all patients with suspected ACS after excluding clinical and ECG signs suggestive of STEMI or very high-risk NSTE-ACS.
key_points: Biomarkers complement diagnosis, risk stratification, and management in suspected ACS.
A rise and/or fall in cTn above the 99th percentile of healthy individuals supports a diagnosis of myocardial infarction (MI) when clinical presentation is compatible with myocardial ischaemia.
In patients with MI, cTn levels rise rapidly (usually within 1 hour when using high-sensitivity assays) after symptom onset and remain elevated for a variable period (usually several days).

Abbreviations (from page footnote).GRACE: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events
